title: The game is a pure C# library; Unity is a rendering shell
context: Agents cannot open the Unity editor and cannot verify work that only compiles inside it. A multi-agent system without verification is parallel hallucination, so the binding constraint on autonomy is how much of the game can be checked without Unity.
decision: Gameplay logic lives in Assets/Core as plain C# with no UnityEngine dependency, taking dt as a parameter and drawing all randomness from a seeded IRng. Assets/Unity holds only MonoBehaviour adapters. Enforced by noEngineReferences in the Core asmdef and by check-core-purity.sh in CI.
consequences: Roughly three quarters of the game is testable in milliseconds with no Unity licence, runs are reproducible from a seed, and headless balance simulation becomes possible. The cost is an adapter layer and the discipline of keeping logic out of MonoBehaviours.
